text: He went back to his room, and the scent of mignonette had gone, leaving only the stale, lifeless smell of old furniture and storage. <break time="0.8s" /> The hope that had burned in him for five months died at last, and he sat staring at the dim yellow light for a long time. <break time="0.8s" /> Then, overcome by despair, he gave up on life itself, and he put out the light and lay down on the bed in the silent dark. <break time="0.8s" /> That night the housekeeper, Missus Purdy, sat in the basement with her friend Missus McCool, and the two landladies shared a can of beer and some gossip. <break time="0.8s" /> I rented my third floor back this evening to a young man, said Missus Purdy, and Missus McCool asked in surprise, And did you tell him about it. <break time="0.8s" /> Rooms, said Missus Purdy, are furnished to be rented, and I did not tell him, and Missus McCool agreed that it was good business sense. <break time="0.8s" /> Missus McCool remembered the pretty young girl who had ended her own life in that very room only a week before, saying that she had a sweet little face. <break time="0.8s" /> She would have been called handsome, as you say, said Missus Purdy, but for that mole she had by her left eyebrow, Do fill your glass again.
